summary: The study investigates the use of a tungsten (W) interlayer deposited via atomic layer deposition (ALD) to enhance the nucleation and smoothness of ultrananocrystalline diamond (UNCD) films. The W interlayer significantly improves the initial nucleation density, reduces surface roughness, and enables the growth of thinner, continuous UNCD films. The ALD process allows for precise control over the W thickness, making it suitable for coating complex surfaces.
evidence: UNCD films were deposited on bare and W-coated Si wafers at 800 /C176 C at a power of 1200 W using a commercial microwave plasma system. W films were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD). ALD offers the advantage of coating complex, non-planar surfaces with monolayer control over the W thickness.
